tools.name: unity_find
tools.description: Semantic search for GameObjects in the currently open Unity scene(s). Use this to find objects in the scene hierarchy by describing what you're looking for. Use "*" to list ALL objects in the scene. For project assets (prefabs, materials, textures, etc.), use your file system tools (Glob, Read) to browse the Assets folder, then unity_asset_info to get detailed information.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find, or "*" to list all objects

limit.description: Maximum results (default: 10, use higher values with "*")

tools.name: unity_asset_info
tools.description: Get detailed information about Unity assets. Pass one or more asset paths to get rich descriptions including: for prefabs (components, hierarchy, materials, vertex count), for materials (shader, colors, textures), for textures (dimensions, format, type), for audio (duration, channels), etc.

paths.description: Asset paths relative to project root (e.g., 'Assets/Prefabs/Player.prefab')

tools.name: unity_execute
tools.description: Execute temporary, one-off C# code in Unity Editor for immediate actions like creating GameObjects, modifying scenes, or querying object properties. The code becomes the body of an AIExecute() method. Use Debug.Log() for output. Do NOT use this to write permanent script files - use the Write tool for that, then unity_compile_permanent_script to compile.

code.description: C# code to execute (temporary, not saved)

tools.name: unity_compile_permanent_script
tools.description: After writing permanent C# script file(s) (MonoBehaviour, ScriptableObject, etc.) using the Write tool, call this to trigger import. This will cause Unity to recompile, which temporarily disconnects the server. After calling this, poll unity_check_compile_status until compilation is complete before using the new script types.

script_paths.description: Path(s) to script files relative to project root (e.g., ['Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs', 'Assets/Scripts/EnemyAI.cs'])

tools.name: unity_check_compile_status
tools.description: Check if Unity is currently compiling scripts. Call this after unity_compile_permanent_script to poll until compilation is complete. Returns status: 'compiling' (still working), 'updating' (asset database updating), 'ready' (success - can use AddComponent), or 'error' (compilation failed with errors shown). If 'error', fix the script and try again.

tools.name: unity_scene_view
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the Unity Scene view. By default the screenshot includes the editor gizmos the user is currently seeing (selection outlines, colliders, custom Handles, etc.). Optionally move the Scene view camera first by framing a GameObject (`look_at`) or by setting `pivot` / `rotation_euler` / `size` directly. Use this to visually inspect the scene, verify object placement, confirm edits, or debug layout issues. Returns an image block you can see.

look_at.description: GameObject name to frame in the Scene view. Uses the object's renderer bounds, or falls back to position. Partial case-insensitive match.

pivot.description: World-space pivot point the camera orbits [x, y, z]. Ignored if look_at is set.

rotation_euler.description: Camera euler rotation in degrees [x, y, z]. Ignored if look_at is set.

size.description: Scene view zoom / distance from pivot. Smaller = closer. Ignored if look_at is set.

restore_view.description: If true (default), restore the Scene view to its previous pivot/rotation/size after the screenshot so the user's camera isn't hijacked. Set false to leave the camera where you moved it. Ignored when no camera move params are provided.

show_gizmos.description: If true (default), include editor gizmos in the screenshot — matches what the user is currently seeing in the Scene view. Set false to capture a clean render with no gizmos, handles, or selection outlines.
